findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117: align-items() omits -moz-box-align although the display mixins enable -moz-box, causing Firefox versions using that fallback to ignore requested centering and baseline alignment. Add -moz-box-align: $alignment.

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117: align-items() omits -moz-box-align although the display mixins enable -moz-box, causing Firefox versions using that fallback to ignore requested centering and baseline alignment. Add -moz-box-align: $alignment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the `inline-flex()` mixin includes `-moz-box` and `-moz-inline-box` display values for Firefox fallback compatibility. However, looking at the `align-items()` mixin at lines 117-122, it includes `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items`, but is missing `-moz-box-align`. This is inconsistent - if the display mixins support the old Mozilla flexbox syntax (-moz-box), then the align-items mixin should also include the corresponding -moz-box-align property for those older Firefox versions to properly handle alignment.
